headline: Topsfield Fair pumpkin record falls to 2,598-pound gourd
dek: Woody Lancaster of Topsfield won the 42nd All New England Giant Pumpkin Weigh-Off in his final competition, surpassing last year’s fair record by 91 pounds.
body: A Topsfield grower ended his competitive giant-pumpkin career by setting a new record at the fair that helped make the sport a New England fall tradition. Woody Lancaster’s 2,598-pound pumpkin won the 42nd All New England Giant Pumpkin Weigh-Off on Oct. 2, according to the [Topsfield Fair’s official results](https://www.topsfieldfair.org/about/press/) and independent reporting by [The Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/02/metro/woody-lancaster-topsfield-fair-giant-pumpkin/).

The result was a 91-pound improvement over the previous Topsfield Fair mark. Alex Noel of Abington, Connecticut, set that record with a 2,507-pound pumpkin in 2025; Lancaster’s entry moved the fair’s winning benchmark above 2,500 pounds for the second consecutive year. The Globe reported that 21 pumpkins were entered and that Lancaster, 80, had said this would be his final weigh-off after decades of growing.

The victory carried both a local connection and a regional field. Lancaster grows his pumpkins in Topsfield and has served as a longtime co-chair of the fair’s signature opening-night event. The runner-up, Larry and Shauna Masters, entered a 2,220-pound pumpkin from just over the Massachusetts line in New York. Joe Jutras of North Scituate, Rhode Island, placed third with a 2,197-pound entry, while John and Kerry Young of Jericho, Vermont, finished fourth at 1,876 pounds, the Globe reported.

The competition also highlighted a younger grower. Eleven-year-old Alistair Lehto of Fitchburg, Massachusetts, placed fifth with an 1,815-pound pumpkin and received $500 as junior grower of the year. The result gives the event a local youth angle at a moment when veteran growers are aging out. The Globe reported that Lancaster has mentored Henry Swenson, a 24-year-old Topsfield grower whose pumpkin weighed 1,246 pounds this year after disease hurt the crop.

The scale numbers are the culmination of a season-long project, not a quick fair stunt. Lancaster told the Globe that his winning pumpkin was pollinated in July, gained roughly 58 pounds a day and benefited from a different fertilizer mix in his last year. The paper reported that he can spend as much as four hours a day on the hobby. Those details help explain why the weigh-off is treated as a serious agricultural contest even though the winning fruit is also a crowd-pleasing spectacle.

Topsfield’s event has deeper roots than the current record. The fair says the All New England Giant Pumpkin Weigh-Off began in 1984, when the winner weighed 433 pounds. The New England Giant Pumpkin Growers Association later made Topsfield its official weigh-off site, and the contest now requires entries to weigh at least 300 pounds. The fair’s history notes that a 2,480-pound pumpkin set the previous record in 2022, before the 2025 and 2026 jumps.

The Topsfield mark is not the same as the world record. [WBUR’s preview of this year’s event](https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/10/02/topsfield-fair-giant-pumpkins-record) reported that the global mark stood at 2,819 pounds after a 2025 entry in England. Lancaster’s result is therefore a fair record and a New England agricultural milestone, but it does not establish a new world best.

The winning pumpkin and four runners-up will remain on display through the Topsfield Fair’s closing day on Oct. 12, according to the Globe. For the fair, the record adds a headline attraction to an 11-day event that opened with the weigh-off. For Lancaster, it is a final competitive chapter: a hometown grower, at the fair’s central agricultural contest, finishing with the largest pumpkin the venue has ever weighed.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Topsfield Fair pumpkin record set at 2,598 pounds
